skill.name: machine-learning-ops-ml-pipeline
skill.description: Plan production MLOps pipelines with data, training, deployment, Kubernetes, monitoring, and continuous improvement guidance.
skill.summary: Design end-to-end machine learning operations pipelines for production systems.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The two static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and a deployment option list. I found no prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or unsafe command execution in the reviewed SKILL.md content.

static_findings.snippet: - If detailed examples are required, open `resources/implementation-playbook.md`.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 25 uses Markdown backticks around a resource path for documentation. It is not Ruby execution, shell execution, or a command invocation.
Line 270 lists deployment modes such as realtime, batch, streaming, and hybrid. This is configuration guidance, not host or network reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Production ML systems require coordinated data, training, deployment, and monitoring plans. This skill structures that work into practical MLOps phases.
actual_capabilities: Breaks ML pipeline planning into data, modeling, deployment, Kubernetes, and monitoring phases.
Guides data quality, lineage, feature store, and storage architecture decisions.
Plans training workflows with experiment tracking, registries, validation, and rollback procedures.
Outlines serving infrastructure, CI/CD gates, infrastructure as code, and secret management.
Defines monitoring coverage for drift, latency, quality, alerts, costs, and retraining triggers.
limitations: Provides planning and implementation guidance, not automatic cloud provisioning.
Requires project data sources, target metrics, and operational constraints from the user.
Generated designs need review by data, platform, and security teams before production use.
Does not replace load testing, model validation, or compliance approval.

use_cases.title: Plan a New MLOps Platform
use_cases.description: Create an end-to-end blueprint for data ingestion, training, serving, monitoring, and retraining.

use_cases.title: Standardize Model Delivery
use_cases.description: Turn ad hoc notebooks into repeatable pipelines with experiment tracking, model registry, and deployment gates.

use_cases.title: Improve Production Reliability
use_cases.description: Add monitoring, drift detection, rollback, and cost controls to existing model serving workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Pipeline Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a new machine learning project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production ML pipeline for a churn prediction model. Include data ingestion, training, deployment, monitoring, and success criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Tooling Selection
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an MLOps pipeline for real-time recommendations using AWS, MLflow, Feast, Kubernetes, and Prometheus. Explain each major tooling choice.

prompt_templates.title: Migration Roadmap
prompt_templates.scenario: Move from notebooks to automated production workflows.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration plan from notebook-based model development to automated pipelines with versioned data, model registry, CI/CD, and monitoring.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced Operating Model
prompt_templates.scenario: Define a full production operating model.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a multi-cloud MLOps operating model with feature stores, canary releases, drift alerts, retraining triggers, incident runbooks, and cost controls.

output_examples.input: Design an MLOps pipeline for fraud detection with batch training and real-time inference.
output: A phased architecture covering data ingestion, quality checks, feature store design, model training, deployment, and monitoring.
Recommended tools for experiment tracking, model registry, serving, orchestration, and drift detection.
Operational criteria for latency, uptime, rollback, retraining, and alert response.

output_examples.input: Improve an existing ML service that has no model monitoring or rollback process.
output: A monitoring plan for data drift, model quality, latency, throughput, and business impact.
A deployment strategy with canary releases, automated rollback, and validation gates.
A runbook outline for incident response, retraining triggers, and ownership handoffs.

best_practices: Provide concrete data sources, target metrics, latency needs, and deployment constraints before using the skill.
Review generated architecture with data engineering, platform, security, and model owners.
Validate all proposed infrastructure, monitoring thresholds, and rollback steps in a staging environment.
anti_patterns: Do not use generic defaults when data volume, privacy rules, or latency targets are unknown.
Do not deploy generated pipeline code without tests, secrets review, and infrastructure review.
Do not treat model accuracy as the only success metric for production readiness.

faq.question: Does this skill write a complete ML pipeline automatically?
faq.answer: It provides structured plans, implementation guidance, and component recommendations. Teams still need to implement and verify the final system.

faq.question: Which tools does it cover?
faq.answer: It references common MLOps tools such as MLflow, Weights and Biases, Feast, KServe, Seldon, Kubeflow, Airflow, and Prometheus.

faq.question: Can it support cloud-specific designs?
faq.answer: Yes. The prompt can include AWS, Azure, GCP, or multi-cloud constraints for platform-specific recommendations.

faq.question: Is this useful for early prototypes?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create a lightweight path from prototype to production while identifying which controls can wait.

faq.question: Does it handle monitoring and drift detection?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow includes model performance, data drift, concept drift, alerts, dashboards, and retraining triggers.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
